articleTitle: Analysis of a WPT system in terms of coupling factor and compliance with magnetic flux density limits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The aim of this work is to investigate a Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system in different configurations from the perspective of human exposure to the electromagnetic field at close range. For this purpose, the guidelines of the ICNIRP (International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection) and the IEEE/ICES (International Committee on Electromagnetic Safety) were followed. Furthermore, the efficiency aspect is taken into account for the evaluation of the coupling factor for different scenarios. A 3D model was created and simulated by using FEM software. The results of the simulation provide information on the positioning and design of a suitable shielding with high transmission efficiency and offer a suggestion for potential material savings.

articleTitle: Technical limitations of Organic Human-Robot Interaction (O-HRI) for mobile robots moving amongst humans
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: There is a growing need to make human-robot interaction natural. Its principles were summarized by psychologists under the name O-HRI. If we want to extend the O-HRI concept to mobile robots moving between people, then the most important feature is the indication of intent. The robot can indicate its intention with micro-movements; e.g. if a person comes up against the robot, it indicates in advance with a micro-movement where it will turn. Micromovements have limitations, both on the human streets of perception and on the robot side in technical execution. The most important parameters are the temporal and spatial length of the micromovement, as well as the maximum acceleration. This paper focuses on the technical possibilities and limitations, which help psychologists in what can be technically implemented in robots from human subconscious intent signals in human-human interaction.

Author Keywords: Technical limitation of movement of a mobile robot

articleTitle: Bond Graph Benefits the Education in Mechatronics Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper provides a novel graphical Bond Graph teaching method to benefit the education quality in mechatronics engineering. Mechatronics engineering is considered an interdisciplinary subject since it involves mechanical, electronics, and control theory. Traditional control engineering focuses on dynamic mathematics modeling, such as state-space and ordinary differential equations, which makes it difficult to understand the subjects’ concepts during education. This paper proposes the Bond Graph as a native language for mechatronics engineering students, which can reach the same result as the traditional transfer function and state space methods with slight differences in modeling concepts. The Bond Graph also has a synergy property by representing multiple domains using the same toolset language. The Bond Graph as a Dataflow program helps students digest the complexity of the concept because of its modular characteristics. The Bond Graph provides convenience in mechatronics engineering education from a pure graphical modeling method.

articleTitle: Modification of the Clarke Transformation Matrices for Controlling Electric Machines with Non-Equally Spaced Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The Clarke transformation is mathematically a Vandermonde matrix of a discrete Fourier transformation. Its purpose is to transform space-vector quantities in the space domain. One necessary condition is that the base function forms an n-th root of unity. This condition translates into requiring all sampling points to be equally spaced. However, manufacturing constraints and imperfections in electric machines may result in non-equally spaced magnetic axes, especially in the case of multiphase electrical machines, making the conventional inverse Clarke transformation used in classic vector control inaccurate. The mathematical inverse Clarke transformation solves this issue, and the existence of this matrix is always ensured. This avoids additional control action and for model predictive controllers, an accurate model is crucial. Analytical results and a simple experimental validation on a multiphase induction machine show the improvements introduced by changing the transformation matrix.

articleTitle: Study on Rotor Position Detection Implementation for On-the-fly Start-up Technique of a PMSM Drive without a Position Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper describes a technique for the on-the-fly start-up of a permanent magnet synchronous motor without a position sensor. The technique uses resistive voltage divider sensors on motor phases usually built-in integrated drivers, thus no additional sensors are needed. The rotor position at speed is detected and monitored even if the power inverter is not activated. A smooth transition to active drive is enabled, removing the complete stop and align phase from the usual start-up sequence.

articleTitle: Power Grid Current Harmonics Reduction and Voltage Balancing with 5-Level CHB Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Active filters, essential components of power grid infrastructure, play a crucial role in enhancing the quality of electrical energy. This paper proposes a control strategy design for an active filter consisting of three 5-level cascaded H-bridge converters. The proposed control strategy is based on a finite control set model predictive control, for which a comprehensive mathematical model of the system is developed. Power grid analysis, which is inevitable for the active filter proper function, is conducted using the PQ theory, which computes instantaneous active and reactive power. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated through a detailed set of simulations, and the sensitivity of model parameters is observed. The proposed system is compared with a 3-level topology to highlight its advantages.

articleTitle: Development of Meta-Heuristic Optimization Based Control of Redesigned VW Crafter Hybrid Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper uses the MATLAB/Simulink/Simscape environment to evaluate the performance of a conventional Volkswagen (VW) Crafter, equipped with a 6-speed manual gearbox and a 2.0 Turbocharged Direct Injection Common Rail Diesel (TDI CR) engine, which is converted into a hybrid vehicle. A parallel hybrid vehicle powered by a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is compared to the conventional version. A genetic algorithm (GA) is applied to tune the classical PID controller to optimize energy consumption. A novel methodology is also introduced based on the hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) method, leveraging an online data acquisition (DAQ) system integrated into the vehicle’s Controller Area Network (CAN Bus) system. The acquired CAN bus data is analyzed using LabVIEW and Net CAN plus 110 hardware. The simulated vehicle demonstrates better performance than the real vehicle based on the comparison between the simulation and experimental results. The transformed hybrid vehicle achieves 75.11% reduction in fuel consumption and an energy efficiency of 84.62%.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Wide Voltage Range Series-Parallel Resonant Buck-Boost DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper explores the possibility for the buck-boost series-parallel resonant current-source converter (SPR-CSC) to be adopted for bidirectional operation. Due to the presence of a parallel capacitor, the conventional modulation approaches cannot be directly applied for reverse operation mode. To address this, two new modulation techniques are developed that create zero voltage switching (ZVS) conditions and avoid the capacitive loading of the transistors during turn-on. The modulations allow the converter to operate in both buck and boost modes and additionally take advantage of voltage range extension using a reconfigurable full- / half-bridge circuit. The operational modes are described and verified using a 3.3 kW model of the converter that interfaces 350 VDC and 200…800 VDC sources. An analysis of stresses on converter components is given to assess the impact and additional requirements introduced when adopting the topology to bidirectional operation.

articleTitle: Addressing Cross-Coupling Issues in Magnetically Integrated Three-Port DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: DC grid-forming converters are used to provide dc power distribution inside buildings. Often, such converters are based on dual-active bridge (DAB) technology to provide high-frequency isolation. Certain developing standards related to dc installations specify different isolation classes and protection zones. This is a critical requirement for power converter design, especially for building applications where end-users are close to the loads, and it is necessary to provide extra safety. To comply with these requirements, isolation is needed between the primary DC buses (700 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf>), dc power distribution buses (320-380 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf>), and extra-low voltage levels (24-60 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf>), where loads are connected. Three-port converters are a potential solution for this application to reduce the number of power processing stages. However, when working under droop control at the output, magnetic cross-coupling issues must be addressed. In this paper, a three-port isolated dc-dc converter is described and analyzed, verifying the influence of magnetic cross-coupling on the extra-low voltage port, which is usually not regulated. To experimentally verify this proposal, a 5.3 kW prototype was built, and laboratory tested, comparing different transformer designs.

articleTitle: Multi-Verse Optimizer as a Tool for Efficiency Improvement of Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes an application of a novel nature-inspired algorithm called Multi-Verse Optimizer (MVO) in the efficiency improvement of a permanent magnet motor. This algorithm is based on the following three main inspirations in cosmology: white hole, black hole, and wormhole. The mathematical presentation of these three concepts is implemented in order to perform exploration, exploitation, and local search on the search area, respectively. In this work this algorithm is used to perform an optimal design on a permanent magnet motor where the inverse value of the efficiency of the motor is defined as an objective function. Comparative analysis of the initial and the optimized motor model is performed using the data from the optimization as well as from the performed Finite Element Analysis for the investigated models.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of an Axial Five Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper deals with design of a five phase axial permanent magnet synchronous machine. The analytical design is verified by finite element analysis of designed topology. A prototype of designed machine is manufactured and measured in no-load state and under various loads.

articleTitle: Open-Source Internal Signal Analysis Unit for FPGA Paired With Rust Real-Time Monitor GUI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: To address the gap in the tooling software for verifying Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) design, this paper introduces a Verilog implementation of a fully synthesizable unit for monitoring values of internal wires and registers. The unit samples an arbitrary number of internal signals and packages them into a Universal Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter (UART) message. Even when analysing multiple bit values only three FPGA board pins are required to transmit and receive messages using UART, in contrast to the conventional hardware logic analyzers where numerous pins are needed. The message is then sent from the FPGA to the Real-Time Monitor (RTM) application running on a host PC. Developed using the Rust programming language, the application ensures reliability, performance, memory safety, and efficiency. The resource utilization of the unit, deployed on the Gowin GW1NR-9 27 MHz chip, is presented. The unit, along with the RTM application, can be efficiently utilized for verifying arbitrary Verilog designs or employing them as an acquisition or monitoring hardware-software product.

articleTitle: Voltage Distortion Effects in GaN-Based Dual-Inverters Caused by Deadtime and Delayed Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper investigates the most significant voltage distortion effects present in GaN-based Dual Inverter (DI) topology. Dual Inverters have emerged as promising solutions for various applications in electric drives, offering advantages such as superior DC-bus voltage utilization and multilevel operation capability. These advantages can be further enhanced when equipped with wide bandgap power devices such as GaN. However, despite the superior switching speeds of GaN devices compared to their traditional Si counterparts, they still exhibit nonlinear behavior and delayed current-dependent switching properties, resulting in distortion in the inverter output voltage, especially in high-frequency applications. Therefore, this paper aims to analyze and analytically describe the output voltage distortion arising from deadtime and delayed switching in GaN-based DIs. A simple mathematical model is proposed to accurately characterize this type of voltage distortion, which is then experimentally validated using a custom laboratory DI prototype.

articleTitle: Python-LTSpice Framework for Impact Study of PCB Parasitics on Conducted Emission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This work presents a circuit pre-processing framework for LTSpice to identify main contributors to the common-mode conducted emission spectrum by iterative Python-controlled simulation, applying One-at-a-time sampling. For demonstration, a flyback DC/DC converter and the automotive CISPR25 measurement standard are used. The contribution of PCB parasitic capacitances to the CM emission spectrum is analyzed, as well as capacitive components of flyback transformer, SiC transistor switch and cable harness. The frequency range under consideration is CISPR band B and C from 150 kHz to 300 MHz.

articleTitle: Impact of Coordinate System Selection and Model Observability on Position Sensorless State Estimation of Nonsalient-Pole PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Model observability is essential for the design of state estimators and observers, since the state vector can only be fully reconstructed from the measurements, if the model is observable. However, some research articles do not perform observability analysis and use unobservable models, while the presented results show adequate estimation performance. This paper deals with the impact of observability on the position sensorless state estimation of nonsalient-pole permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM). To show how the observability depends on the chosen coordinate system, observability studies are presented for two widely used nonlinear state-space models given in either the stator or the rotor reference frame. For the stationary reference frame model, a necessary and sufficient observability condition is defined, and it is shown that the model using rotor-oriented variables is unobservable. To point out the limitations of using the unobservable model, comparative simulations are carried out between extended Kalman filters using the models presented.

articleTitle: An improved Bidirectional Hybrid Switched-Inductor Switched-Capacitor Converter Topology with Wide Voltage Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes an improvement to a bidirectional hybrid switched-inductor switched-capacitor converter (BHSISC), which had theoretical advantages but presented voltage oscillations and PWM frequency voltages between the two inputs. Because of the combination of switched capacitor and switched inductor cells, the converter achieved a wider voltage conversion ratio between the high voltage (VH) and the low voltage inputs (VL), smaller passive components, and a lower switch stress. Because of parasitic capacitors of the switches the inductive cell present voltage oscillations, which increased the voltage stress on the switches and increased EMI. Another reason for increasing the EMI for the initial topology was the high frequency between the inputs. The new proposed topology eliminates the above-mentioned issues while maintaining the advantages.

articleTitle: Dead Time Adaptive Control for Efficiency Improvement of GaN Transistor Based SPWM Modulated Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Application of GaN transistors into design of three phase inverter can increase the efficiency. Further increase in efficiency can be achieved if the dead time is optimized since GaN transistors have higher voltage drop in reverse conduction region. The paper proposes adaptive change of dead time value during the period of sinusoidal current since optimal dead time depends on load current. Based on LT Spice simulation model and experimental measurements optimal dead time values at different load currents have been determined and look up table for implementation into microcontroller has been created. GaN based inverter was tested with adaptive dead time control pulses. Thermal measurements and simulation results show improvement of the efficiency of the inverter. The temperature of the transistors was reduced by 2 degrees Celsius after implementation of adaptive dead time.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of the General the Dual and the Joint Extended Kalman Filter on State Estimation of Li-ion Battery Cells for BMS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The aim of the work is to compare the performance of the general Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), the joint EKF and the dual EKF for state and parameter estimation of a Samsung 18650INR13L Li-ion battery cell. The used battery model is based on a simplified Randles equivalent circuit equipped with R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ct</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dl</inf> parameters. The initial values of Randles parameters were identified from constant charge, discharge and transient discharge measurements. The performance of the implemented Kalman Filters were compared for the state and parameter estimation of the cell during WLTP test condition. While the general EKF uses only the identified initial values of the parameters, the joint and dual EKF are able to estimate them to compensate for the drift during the operation which leads to more accurate state estimation and compensates the parameters change due to heat and the aging of the cell. From the SOC estimation performance comparison we found out that both the dual and joint EKF perform similarly well, but the dual EKF has about 22% less computational cost which is very significant in the case of the future implementation on a real Battery Management System (BMS) which was the target of this investigation.

articleTitle: Online Education of Microcontroller Control of Electric Drives with FPGA Based HIL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The pandemic situation related to Covid-19 exposed the need for alternative directions in education and its adaptation to online environment. This is especially the case in practically oriented courses, such as microprocessor control of electric drives. Those are typically strongly linked with the laboratory environment and requires special equipment such as electric motors, power converters, power sources, measurement equipment, embedded microcontrollers etc. The paper presents the tools for distant education of laboratory classes of Microprocessor control of electric drives course by using remote access to personal computers located in a laboratory. The core of the presented tool is a real time model of electric drive implemented in FPGA as a real-time Hardware In the Loop (HIL) simulator. The experimental comparison to the real drive is provided to verify the proposed tool.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Multi-Output Flyback Auxiliary Power Supply for Bipolar DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This article introduces an auxiliary power supply (APS) designed explicitly for bipolar DC grids, utilizing a flyback topology for robust and efficient operation. Central to our design is a high-voltage 3300 V silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET and a planar transformer comprising one primary, one auxiliary, and two secondary windings. This APS uniquely addresses the resilience requirements of bipolar grids by enabling seamless switching between poles in the event of a pole failure, thus maintaining continuous power supply. Control is achieved through the UC3844A integrated circuit from Texas Instruments. The converter’s effectiveness is demonstrated through experimental validations, confirming its suitability for advanced bipolar DC grid applications.

articleTitle: Classification of Rigid Objects from High-Bandwidth Data Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Research in haptics has advanced for additional technologies such as remote operation and VR. Within this field, there’s a growing need for preserving environmental fidelity to achieve higher precision in tactile reproduction. This paper focuses on tactile feedback and discusses object classification inspired by methods for preserving hardness. Identifying the hardness of objects typically requires grasping, which necessitates a certain level of softness; hence, rigid objects cannot be identified. Moreover, when focusing solely on classification, some methods involve chemical techniques or sound-based tests like hammering. However, these methods are not designed for tactile feedback and do not directly correlate with tactile information. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for classifying previously untargeted rigid objects using a scheme similar to that for identifying object hardness. To accomplish this, experiments were conducted using a high-bandwidth data acquisition method with Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The experiment involved identifying objects with similar appearances but differing masses, such as aluminum and iron, and comparing the results.

articleTitle: Analysis of Output Power with Temperature Using Bi-Directional DC Converter in Boost Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In this paper, analysis of output power changes with the change in temperature was explained. The two different DC converters were designed. One converter is Silicon based and other with Silicon Carbide MOSFET’s. These Converters are called Bi-directional DC Converters operating under Boost Mode. The Software used for the simulation of converters was LTSPICE.

articleTitle: Speed and Torque Model Predictive Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper presents a finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Compared to the commonly presented approaches, here both speed and current controllers are based on predictive formulas. The load torque observer is applied to ensure disturbance compensation. The novelty of the proposed solution lies in the designed cost function, where additional components were introduced to provide high-performance operation of the drive. This article also presented researches results about impact different values of cost function components reinforcements where this aspect was skipped in similar articles. Experimental tests were carried out to evaluate the performance of the developed control algorithm, focusing on angular velocity regulation, load torque compensation, as well as current and velocity ripples. The proposed solution were compared to the reference one, namely cascade control structure with PI current and speed controllers.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Passive Magnetic Energy Harvesters Operating Under High Primary Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Magnetic energy harvesters (MEHs) are highly reliable devices employed to supply low-power DC loads from high AC current carrying conductors. Recent literature provided means for estimating the input power of a MEH feeding a constant voltage load (CVL) via an uncontrolled rectifier. The goal of the paper is to quantify the different types of losses and thus the conversion efficiency and output power of clamped-type MEHs. Analytical expressions for losses in the magnetic core, secondary winding, and rectifier diodes are developed, in relation to circuit variables. It is shown that the total losses can be considerable, leading to an efficiency in the order of 83%. The analytical predictions demonstrate close resemblance with corresponding results obtained by a passive MEH harvesting ~218 W from a conductor carrying 200 – 300 A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf>.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Suppression Control Considering Magnetic Saturation in Position Sensorless Control with Extended Induced Voltage for IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Several torque ripple suppression controls for interior permanent magnet synchronous motors have been explored due to undesired effects of torque ripple on mechanical systems, including increased vibration and noise. Two distinct controls exist for torque ripple suppression: a method utilizes a torque meter to measure the torque ripple and reduce it directly. Another method involves using a mathematical model to estimate the torque ripple and mitigate its effect. Additionally, position sensorless methods, such as extended induced voltage or adaptive control, have been proposed. However, research on torque ripple suppression control with position sensorless control remains limited. Then, this paper proposes a novel method to enhance position estimation accuracy using q-axis inductance estimation. Notably, the proposed method requires simple controller modification and pre-measurement data; it relies solely on pre-obtained data used in the torque ripple suppression control. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves approximately a 40% reduction in 6th-order torque ripple.

articleTitle: The Inductive External Low-frequency Sensor of Electromagnetic Field using AME 3D PCB Nanotechnology for Biophysics Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The study deals with the human body´s electromagnetic interferences (EMI). The preliminary fundamental theory is put on the designing and modelling small low-frequency inductive electromagnetic field sensors. The possibilities of printed circuit board (PCB) nanotechnology for applications in biophysics are also presented. The aim is to define the limits of this new principle in clinical research. This paper implies methods of modelling and simulation of the sensor concerning recent trends in electronic design.

Author Keywords: external electromagnetic induction in living tissue

articleTitle: Electric Resonance Effects in Electric Machines – How to Measure Them?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Windings of electric machines contain several series and parallel resonances. With steadily increasing switching frequencies in drive applications, the probability of resonance excitation by converter harmonics increases. For rotating electric machines in resonance condition, abnormally high voltages causing insulation premature ageing can occur within the winding. To safely avoid such resonance conditions, the knowledge of resonance positions is necessary. Consequently, impedance curves have to at least be calculated or measured prior to commissioning. Knowledge of internal voltage gains and transfer functions are also highly desirable. This means that appropriate measuring devices have to be available and suitable measuring configurations defined. This paper deals with the verification of a vector network analyzer for the characterisation of a medium-sized traction motor. For typical saturation levels of the magnetic circuit it is additionally shown that the experimentally obtained transfer functions can be utilised for the recalculation of internal voltages and therefore determining of motor insulation stress.

articleTitle: Model-Free Predictive Control for PMSM Incorporating Flux-weakening
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In recent years, permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) have gained significant attention across various industrial sectors, particularly in transportation, owing to their distinct advantages over alternative motor technologies. Notably, PMSMs exhibit higher power density and possess the potential for wide flux weakening operation, thereby extending the speed range of operation—a critical attribute in electric vehicle applications. However, the sensitivity of PMSM control approaches to variations in machine parameters presents a notable challenge, as it can lead to degradation in controller performance when discrepancies arise between modeled parameters and real-world conditions. Addressing this concern, this study introduces a model-free adaptation of finite control set (FCS) predictive control (FCS-MFPC) tailored for flux weakening (FW) operation. Through simulation analysis conducted over the US Environmental Protection Agency Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule, the performance of this controller is examined. Additionally, the performance of the controller is compared to conventional FCS-MPC. To facilitate a comprehensive comparison, criteria such as reference tracking error and drive efficiency are considered.

articleTitle: Case Study of BESS Capability for Low-Frequency Power Oscillations Active Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper explores the problem of low-frequency power oscillations (LFO), which has been largely monitored by the deployment of wide-area measurement systems (WAMS). Specifically, there is investigated the potential in the use of a battery energy storage system (BESS) for inter-area LFO active compensation. This can have benefits in grid stability, control, fault immunity, or energy loss reduction. For the applicability evaluation, a simple model of the measured LFO and BESS interaction is developed and a suitable control algorithm for the BESS is proposed. Key challenges for future research regarding LFO compensation are identified in the process. In conclusion, the case study simulation results are discussed and the benefits of the proposed LFO compensation system are evaluated regarding possible alternative solutions.

articleTitle: Parameter Robustness Comparison of Pseudo-Sliding Mode Observer and Extended EMF Observer for Synchronous Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Position control is crucial for the effective operation of synchronous motors, facilitating essential transformations and control strategies. This critical position information is typically acquired through sensors or position observers, which are increasingly utilized in many applications these days. However, the reaction of these observers to motor parameter variations remains uncertain when employed for position determination. In this study, we compare two position observers designed for synchronous reluctance motors in terms of their robustness to motor parameter variations. Our findings reveal that the Extended EMF (EEMF) observer demonstrates superior robustness compared to the Pseudo-Sliding Mode Observer (PSMO) in the face of parameter changes. The PSMO exhibits persistent speed deviations, leading to increased positional errors. Conversely, the EEMF observer effectively mitigates these deviations, closely tracking the motor’s actual speed and position. Our results highlight the EEMF observer’s capability to handle motor parameter changes and uncertainties, positioning it as a more effective choice for reliable motor control applications.

articleTitle: Optimal Current Setpoints for Five-Phase Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Maximum torque per current (MTPA) and other optimal curves have been recently extended to multiphase machines. Since multiphase machines have more degrees of freedom than their three-phase counterparts, the solution exhibits many more regimes of optimal control. In this paper, we study the optimal current setpoints for a five-phase induction machine. Due to missing flux from permanent magnets, the operating regimes differ from those of synchronous machines. Namely, the optimal position of the third harmonic is often symmetric with the first. Hence, the number of regimes is lower than that of the synchronous machine.

articleTitle: Active motor terminal overvoltage mitigation method for parallel voltage source inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Motor terminal overvoltage, which is caused by a long motor cable, is a common issue in industrial drives. This oscillating overvoltage can be dealt with by reinforcing winding insulation, yet it will still be a source for electromagnetic interference. Also, the voltage transition rates at the motor terminals may cause other adverse effects, especially when they also contribute to the common-mode voltage waveform. This paper proposes a du/dt filtering method that is dedicated for parallel connected inverters. The proposed method uses an intercell transformer between the parallel phase outputs to limit the circulating current. The leakage inductances of the transformer windings are then used to form an LC low-pass filter, along with an output capacitor. The method uses an interleaved PWM pattern to actively damp the oscillation that would be generated by the switching behavior and the LC circuit. This paper demonstrates the operation of the proposed du/dt filtering method by simulations.

articleTitle: LCL-Filtered Grid-Tied Inverter with FCS-MPC Based on FAS Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC) based on a Fully Actuated System (FAS) model for an LCL-filtered grid-tied inverter. The grid-connected inverter with an LCL filter is analyzed. The proposed controller only measures the grid current, the inverter current, and the grid voltage. It does not require measurement or estimation of capacitor voltage and current, which is an advantage over the usual use of the state-space model where capacitor current or voltage, or both, must be measured or estimated. The main advantage of using the FAS model is that the implementation is simplified and the number of sensors used is reduced. In addition, a different Cost Function (CF) is proposed which offers good performance. The system is analyzed and designed, and simulation results are shown to validate the proposed system. This paper contributes to improving grid-tied systems with advanced control techniques that must meet the growing demand for electric power.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Partial Power Converter for Beer Brewing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The defossilization of industrial processes is currently one of the main efforts at stopping the climate crisis. In particular, the beer industry has been looking at electrifying its heat-dependent processes to reduce its carbon footprint. Yet, current solutions are typically tailored for large-scale breweries leaving microbreweries, due to a larger relative cost, to use gas as primary resource, which makes it difficult to control the process temperature. To ensure a fine temperature control, thus avoid malt’s stress, a dc-powered heating element can be used. Yet, the cost of this solution is still not suitable for microbreweries. In this paper, we propose the use of a reconfigurable partial-power converter that allows to increase the overall power rating while maximizing its efficiency, together with a full-bridge rectifier that controls the dc-link voltage and ensures low harmonic-content. The simulation results show that the control scheme is capable of reconfiguring the partial-power converter to seamlessly transition between a flyback mode to a step-down partial-power converter mode only when full heating power is needed, thus allowing to shrink the cost of the overall system.

articleTitle: Simultaneous, Coordinated and Centralized Control of Fast Charging Stations and Advanced Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The insertion of fast charging stations (FCSs) and distributed energy resources (DERs) aggravates technical issues in the electrical power system, such as variations in the point of common coupling (PCC) voltage profile and overload on feeders. Ancillary services provided by these elements help to reduce these issues and microgrid (μG) control algorithms coordinate these ancillary services. However, microgrid control studies focus on solutions that do not simultaneously coordinate FCSs and DERs, nor the coordination of advanced microgrids and FCSs. This paper proposes a coordinated and simultaneous control of FCSs and advanced microgrids. The results show that the proposed method performs the ancillary services of valley filling and peak shaving in a minigrid (MG) (i.e., a set of advanced microgrids, FCSs and others). This method allows the voltage profile to be maintained at appropriate levels, ensuring the commitment to vehicle recharging and the independence of the advanced microgrid.

articleTitle: Control Based on FGS-PID for Modular Multiport DC/DC Converter in Multi-Energy Storage Barge System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of multiple energy sources, including Lithium-Ion Batteries (LIBs), Vanadium Redox Flow Batteries (VRFBs), and Fuel cells, within charging stations designed for various vessels and cruise ships. Multiport Modular Multilevel Converters (MP-MMC) have been suggested to address this necessity, surpassing the performance, efficiency, and reliability of multiple SISO DC/DC converters. Despite these benefits, the presence of cross-coupling between control variables poses a significant challenge in designing controllers for MP-MMC. This paper provides an in-depth model of an MP-MMC and presents a control strategy employing a Fuzzy Gain Scheduling of PID (FGS-PID) controller.

articleTitle: End of life influencing factors for Dual Active Bridge components in Flow Battery Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This article discusses the various ways in which the stresses experienced by the IGBTs and diodes in a Dual Active Bridge (DAB) are asymmetric. This asymmetry can be between the two bridges or between IGBTs and diodes on both bridges. The terminal voltage, transformer ratio and the power through the DAB are varied to discuss the stresses. These asymmetrical stresses lead to devices’ distinct temperatures. This unevenness of stresses can affect the lifetime of the devices employed. An analytical model of the DAB is used to analyse the currents and power losses in various devices. Some preliminary results of power losses in the devices are presented.

articleTitle: Study of electrical energy coupling between turbine and compressor in gas-cooled small modular reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The system of electrical transfer of energy between the turbo-system in the secondary circuit and main circulating compressor in the primary circuit of a small modular nuclear reactor has been proposed and simulated with regard to the energy balance and reliability to ensure the proper functioning in standard operation and also during run-down of this gas-cooled reactor. A simplified model has been also compiled to make identification of basic dynamic and power properties of this complicated system very quick even in longer time scales.

articleTitle: Compensation strategies of electric arc furnace with ability to detect cyber-attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The contribution describes an attempt to implement a cyber attack detection system based on the watermark strategy into the system of compensation elements for the EAF. The strategy of the power-electronics-based emulation of the EAF developed before is used here for implementation of the watermark strategy. The developed emulation strategy enables the real-time emulation of the EAF with its under-scaled control components in various modes of operation in laboratory conditions. Selected results of simulation tests using the data collected from the real 60 t EAF are presented and discussed.1 The simulation results confirm that the watermark strategy may be an effective tool to recognize cyber-attacks on the compensation strategy of the EAF.

Author Keywords: simulation using data from steel factory

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of DC-link using Reduced Order Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: In the field of automotive component evaluation and verification, cost considerations play a pivotal role in the development of electrical devices. To address this, we propose to use virtual release techniques and integrating simulation through model order reduction methods. By doing so, we can efficiently reduce costs and testing durations. In this context, we demonstrate crucial steps involved in defining the entire process, specifying simulation requirements, and implementing this approach. Our focus is on building an inverter model capable of predicting transient temperature behavior of the DC-link with quantified accuracy, achieved through a combination of Finite Volume Method and Reduced Order Modeling methods. The techniques for verification and calibration are addressed. The process of validation using statistical methods is elaborated.

articleTitle: Project Based Learning Activities as a Tool for Efficient Education in Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Education of engineers entering to Hi-Tech industry requires application of novel methods and approaches, ensuring understanding not only principles of knowledge, but also organization of designing process and modern form of team collaboration. This approach is present in education by Project Based Learning (PBL). Recent PBL-based activities performed by students in Lab of Power Electronics at the Silesian University of Technology, shows that this approach brings numerous benefits. PBL as a form of practical education ensure individual approach to student’s expectations and allows to include results of students’ investigation to a research conducted by academic staff. Presented results of realized projects show that the student’s research can be devoted both, to solve new research problems and develop devices and demonstrators dedicated for educational purposes. Idea of Project Based Learning, expected outcomes, range of performed activities and examples of results are presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Rotor Design of a Hybrid-excited PMSM for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper deals with the electromagnetic design of the hybrid-excited rotor for a given stator of existing permanent magnet synchronous motor. The design is intended as an alternative to standard synchronous motors with rare-earth materials. Dimensional restrictions for the design, such as radius and axial length, are given by the existing stator. The topology selection is influenced also by the manufacturing possibility at the university. The design is analyzed using 2D finite element method with respect to torque ripple minimization and total torque maximization. The presented results are for varying DC and AC currents with the goal of identifying maximum DC current rating of the machine. Mechanical and thermal analyses are excluded and will be the subject of investigation in the following work.

articleTitle: Crowbar Overvoltage Protection with Passive Power Supply of Control Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The importance of power semiconductor converters steadily increases and as the use of converters grows, the risk of overvoltage damage also increases. The overvoltage protections are very important parts of electrical equipment containing power converters, e.g. inverters, connected especially to the grid lines. The grid line can originate the transient voltage induced by atmospheric phenomena, etc., which can be transmitted to the power converter. The overvoltage protection based on a mechanical spark system is very robust and simple, but not very precise for set up the break-down voltage. The electronically controlled overvoltage, e.g. crowbar, can operate precisely, but the auxiliary power sources for its control circuit are usually required. This article describes the active crowbar with a passive power supply of its controlled circuits. These control circuits operate directly on the power converter low voltage side and do not require any auxiliary power supply.

articleTitle: Open Phase Condition and its Impact on the Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The article describes the methodology for calculating the heating of an induction machine with an asymmetrical power supply. Parasitic torques and the effect on the machine torque curve are shown. The goal is to determine how long the motor can still be operated with a given voltage asymmetry before the allowable temperature is exceeded.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Single-Phase Integrated On-Board Charger for Ultracapacitor-Battery Based EVs with V2G and Regenerative Braking Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper develops the EV powertrains by introducing a multiport multifunctional integrated charger designed for single-phase systems. As an integrated on-board charger, this system utilizes the stator windings of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) as the rectifier filter. Four distinct winding configurations are employed to achieve torque cancellation during the charging mode. These configurations are elucidated and comprehensively compared in the paper. The innovative multiport structure of the DC-DC stage allows for the incorporation of ultracapacitors as supplementary power storage alongside the battery, thereby augmenting the performance of the hybrid powertrain during acceleration and regenerative braking. This integration makes it possible to extend the battery lifespan. To streamline the powertrain component count, the proposed charger is engineered to operate in five distinct modes: charging, acceleration, driving, regenerative braking, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) functionality. The buck-boost operation of the DC-DC stage across all operational modes enables flexible voltage regulation for the DC-link, Ultracapacitor, and battery. This versatility facilitates optimized charging and discharging processes for both the battery and ultracapacitor, enhancing overall system efficiency. The proposed charger undergoes comprehensive analysis across all modes, with theoretical assessments meticulously validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Adequacy of Hybrid AC-DC Grids with Reliability Oriented Modular Multilevel Converter Design - A Case Study Using Modified RTS-24 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The role of power electronics in advancing electrification and sustainability is pivotal. The Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) is a leading candidate for connecting offshore wind farms to the power grid. However, one of the primary concerns with MMC is its reliability, primarily due to the high number of components, with semiconductors and capacitors being the main sources of failures. This study examines how the modularity and redundancy of the MMC affect its reliability and, consequently, its impact on power system adequacy. Our findings reveal a substantial influence of MMC’s modularity and redundancy on power system adequacy. A high level of modularity with no redundancy leads to the worst-case scenario. On the other hand, lower modularity combined with higher redundancy results in the best scenario for power system adequacy. However, it’s important to note that lower modularity and higher redundancy come with increased capital costs of MMC, representing a trade-off between reliability and affordability that we explore in this paper.

articleTitle: The Summary of Induction Motor Torque Ripple Theories for Motor Torque Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper is focused on the summary of induction motor torque ripple theories which is braked by dynamometer. The main aim of this paper explains the causes of the creations of harmonics components contained in the torque of the induction motor during steady state or dynamic motor operation. Furter point of this paper is separation of torque components between measured motor and dynamometer because the torque is measured by one sensor situated on the same coupled shaft common for both machines. Practical, it is the torque analysis with respect of motor and dynamometer topology and both machines are supplied by sinusoidal source only.

articleTitle: An optimal dual active bridge converter modulation strategy for optimal loss distribution and reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper shows that the state of the art dual active bridge modulation strategies do not distribute the losses evenly on the power semiconductors. When employing MOSFET, only the conduction losses are evenly balanced, when employing IGBT and diodes both conduction and switching losses are unbalanced. The present paper proposes a new modulation method that distributed the losses optimally on the power semiconductors. This allows reducing the peak junction temperature by a significant amount and reducing the overall power semiconductor losses by some non negligible amount. The effectiveness of the scheme is shown in simulation. The feasibility is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: A New Control Strategy of the Solar Buck Battery Charger using the Interleaved Ampere-Sec Balance Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The DC-DC buck converter can be applied to solar photovoltaic (PV) battery charging applications. However, the solar buck battery charger exhibits nonlinear behavior in the output current due to the nonlinear output of the solar PV array and the fixed voltage of the output-side battery. Therefore, this paper analyzes the nonlinearity of the output current from the perspective of Ampere-sec balance in all regions, and proposes interleaved ampere-sec balance control to enhance stability. The modeling of the solar buck battery charger and the solar interleaved buck battery charger employs unified modeling. This enables accurate comparisons, and the improvement in stability is verified through comparative simulations.

articleTitle: A New Three-Level Switched Reluctance Motor Drive for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Multilevel power converters have been investigated to improve system-level performance in switched reluctance motor (SRM) drives used in low-voltage applications including electric vehicles. This paper introduces an eight-leg asymmetric three-level power converter that splits the battery into two banks to generate similar operating modes as the conventional three-level asymmetric converters but with improved performance, reduced size, and cost. Unlike the series-connected single battery bank, the proposed split-battery connection offers flexible control and fault tolerance for the SRM drives. The operating modes for the proposed converter are defined, and a current chopping control scheme is presented. The proposed split-battery-driven converter is compared with the standard two-level asymmetric half-bridge converter, and three-level asymmetric converters in terms of cost, efficiency, torque ripple, and current ripple under different operating conditions. The feasibility of the proposed topology is thoroughly tested using a three-phase 12/16 SRM model in MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Investigation of Weighted FOC of Dual Induction Motor Drives Operating under Heavy Load Imbalance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Electric drives used in subway or tramway applications often employ dual traction induction motors connected in parallel and fed by a single converter due to economical reasons. The control can be oriented to the average or weighted flux and torque of the connected motors, as individual flux and torque control of each motor is not possible. In this paper, the control performance related to the weighted flux oriented control of dual induction motors is investigated. A control singularity of weighted FOC arises if one of the motors loses traction capability while a braking torque current set-point is performed. Under these conditions, if the traction-capable motor reaches a specific speed, the weighted flux oriented control scheme reacts in a particular manner. The main flux of the traction-capable motor is significantly reduced while the traction-incapable motor undergoes a shaft speed reversal. The drive ends up not being able to produce steady braking torque. To the best of authors’ knowledge, this effect has not been reported in literature. The existence and characteristics of the control singularity are found and verified in a simulation model consisting of dual induction motors. An experimental test stand consisting of two traction induction motors connected in parallel and fed by a single converter further consolidates the existence and characteristics of the control singularity.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Multiphase Electric Drives with Reduced-error Slope Term
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The higher complexity of multiphase electric drives (MED) has been recently addressed with Model Predictive Control (MPC). In its standard version, MPC typically seeks for the minimum current error, but it does not consider the individual value of each current term. This procedure allows an eventual divergence of some current terms as long as the total sum remains low, and this requires a compensation of such terms in the next sampling period. Aiming to restrict this phenomenon, this paper suggests considering not only the current errors, but also their tendency. This control version with a reduced-error-slope term is termed REST-MPC, and simulations confirm its ability to simultaneously reduce the total harmonic distortion (THD) of phase currents and the switching frequency in the voltage source converter (VSC).

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of 21700-Type Cylindrical and Pouch Nickel Manganese Cobalt Battery Cells for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis between the Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) chemistry-based 21700 cylindrical and pouch battery cells for Electric Vehicle (EV) applications. The sized battery is seamlessly integrated into the traction chain of the EV and exposed to rigorous testing scenarios to evaluate its performance against predetermined benchmarks. Moreover, a nonlinear robust control approach, synergetic control scheme, is proposed to control the speed of the EV. The presented simulation results indicate the superior performance of the 21700 cylindrical NMC cells over the pouch ones across various metrics, including energy capacity, cost-effectiveness, and compactness. Moreover, the integrated battery system demonstrates its high efficiency in supplying power and energy to the traction chain of the EV. The synergetic control mechanism showcases commendable static and dynamic performance during both acceleration and deceleration phases, thereby underscoring its suitability for EV applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid Velocity/Force Filtered Integral-Proportional Control for Damping of Torsional Vibration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This study introduces a methodology for vibration damping based on hybrid control of velocity (or angular velocity) and force (or torque). The hybrid velocity/force integral-proportional controller is developed using the wave model, which accounts for interferences between traveling and reflected waves that induce vibration. Central to the proposed approach is treating the traveling wave as a state variable and the reflected waves as disturbances, thereby enabling velocity control of the load in a backstepping manner. Furthermore, this study addresses the issue of steady-state deviation under load disturbances by incorporating a high-pass filter into the force integral feedback. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed controller and filter.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Power Curtailment on the Switch of a Solar Boost Converter Under Residential Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The massive deployment of PV systems in residential buildings is causing voltage challenges in low-voltage distribution networks. Worldwide, DSOs started requesting users to curtail power when this is injected back into the grid. Although many commercially available inverters can perform curtailment, the degradation effects of curtailment still have to be investigated. This paper estimated how power curtailment affects the reliability of a boost converter working below MPPT voltages. Using the mission profile method, we determined the conduction and switching losses on the converter switch as the critical component, based on its temperature and current profiles. The results suggest that curtailing the power requires the operation point to move towards lower PV voltages, leading to deeper thermal cycles, therefore reducing the expected lifetime of the converter by up to 80 % for power injection into the grid below 1.5 kW. From the operational perspective, this might require premature replacements compared to operating under MPP conditions, affecting the revenue forecast before the enforcement of curtailment. For power injection above 1.5 kW, the LCoE does not change compared to the case without considering the degradation. However, near zero-injection conditions, the difference in LCoE between considering and not considering replacements increases exponentially up to 135 %.

articleTitle: The Three-Level Zero Harmonic Distortion Grid-Forming Converter: A Practical Filterless Solution for Sinusoidal Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The world is rapidly shifting from centralized power generation to distributed generation (DG) with renewable sources near consumers. This transition enhances voltage and frequency stability in microgrids (MGs) and islanded systems, thanks to inverter-based resources. This work introduces the Three-Level Zero Harmonic Distortion (ZHD) grid-forming converter, which produces a sinusoidal voltage without needing costly and inefficient capacitive filters that can cause resonance issues. By combining harmonic cancellation in a three-winding transformer with Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (SHE PWM), the ZHD converter maintains voltage and frequency delivering sinusoidal waveforms even under nonlinear loads. This paper aims to address the main elements of the Three-Level Zero Harmonic Distortion (ZHD) grid-forming concept, including practical implementation considerations, applicable topologies, and simulation results.

articleTitle: Application of the extended Kalman filter in current sensors fault-tolerant control of the induction motor drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Information about the actual current signal is essential in all modern control structures of induction motor (IM) drives. Unfortunately, stator current sensors (CSs) are prone to failure. Therefore, in this paper, fault-tolerant control (FTC) against current sensor faults for an IM drive is proposed. The detection and compensation of CS faults is based on the extended Kalman filter (EKF). To increase the current estimation performance, the state vector is expanded by the coefficient of change of both resistances of the IM. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for different types of CS faults, such as gain change, offset, saturation, or complete signal loss, and under different operating conditions of the IM drive, including regenerative braking. The short detection time and high quality of stator current reconstruction in a wide range of speed and load torque make the presented solution universal for any IM drive with increased safety requirements.

articleTitle: Sensorless Magnetic Flux Balancing Strategies for Novel Dual Active Bridge Converter ZVS Modulation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Novel Dual Active Bridge Converter (DAB) ZVS modulation schemes are proposed, which switch without adapting the switching frequency or the transformer on the entire operating area at zero voltage. During the start-up and transients where the modulation parameters are adjusted to ensure the desired power transfer, an offset occurs in the magnetic flux of the transformer, which may lead to saturation. This paper proposes sensorless strategies to balance the magnetic flux for the proposed modulation patterns during the start-up and transients. The strategies were verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Conversion Efficiency of Active Magnetic Energy Harvesters Operating Under High Primary Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The paper quantifies power conversion efficiency of clamped-type magnetic energy harvester (MEH), supplying power to constant voltage load (CVL) via controlled rectifier. The MEH is assumed to be clamped around a 50Hz/60Hz power line conductor and the CVL voltage is expected to be several tens of volts, allowing neglecting rectifier switching losses. Consequently, magnetic and conduction losses only are taken into account. Analytical expressions related to circuit variables are developed and experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Online Multi-Layer Perceptron-Based Power Quality Monitoring for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Electric vehicles can cause power quality degradation during the charging and discharging operations of the battery bank in grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) enabled vehicles. Sudden decreases in voltages, overvoltages, and grid interruptions (power quality disturbances or PQDs) have to be identified in order to prevent a major grid failure. This paper proposes a multi-fault classification/monitoring system in a power grid connected converter widely used in the charging/discharging system of electric vehicles; this is achieved by a machine learning classification algorithm called multi-layer perceptron. The main objective of this paper is to develop a neural network that monitors the signals coming from the power grid in real-time and can classify behaviours that may cause a malfunction during the operation. Therefore, this study can be used as a monitoring system that can, in a future, perform corrective or/and preventive actions, ensuring a regular operation when PQDs occur in the power grid.

articleTitle: Geometrical Optimization of Charging Pads for Electric Vehicles Wireless Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of geometric optimization of charging pads for electric vehicle (EV) wireless power supply, focusing on the double-D (DD) coil configuration. The optimization process employs the Finite Element Method (FEM) through the optiSLang tool integrated into the ANSYS software suite, aiming to refine the design of electromagnetic coupling elements. The study seeks to align closely with the proposed electrical parameters by leveraging a sophisticated electromagnetic design while minimizing energy losses. Furthermore, the paper includes empirical measurements conducted on an actual device to validate the theoretical models and optimization outcomes. The findings underscore the potential for enhancing the efficiency and reliability of wireless charging systems for EVs, marking a significant step towards sustainable and user-friendly electric mobility solutions.

articleTitle: Part 3: Design and thermal performance evaluation of 3-phase shared core power inductor for Vienna rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The third part of 3-phase Vienna Rectifier Reference Design is focused to the design, and thermal performance evaluation of the power inductor. On the market we can found a lot of final products which are focused manly for low and medium power (from 100W up to few kW). But if we are designing a power supply with higher power (3 and more kW), an customized solution is needed from more reasons, as high power level, mechanical construction of final products (specific dimensions), or the cooling method – cold plate solution or water cooled chassis is more complex as for air cooled power supplies. This paper provides calculation of the power loss behavior of proposed power inductor alternative, while at the end of the paper, the results of the thermal simulations are presented as well.

articleTitle: Droop Control with Incorporated Dead Zone for Indirect Energy Management in DC Nanogrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper explores the application of DC droop control in residential nanogrid. The authors propose a novel approach for grid connected residential dc nanogrids that adjusts the droop curve of the active front-end converter instead of individual energy storage (ES) units. This method incorporates a dead zone within the droop curve to indirectly manipulate the state of charge (SoC) of ES units and enhance renewable energy self-consumption. The proposed ideas are verified via simulations based on a real dataset recorded in Estonia. The results indicate that adjusting the dead zone size can significantly improve renewables self-consumption but had only marginal effect on the SoC.

articleTitle: Current Sensor Fault Detection and Compensation Based on Single Modified Extended Luenberger Observer for Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Fault-Tolerant Control (FTC) strategies are increasingly being employed in modern drive systems due to high safety requirements. In the case of induction motor (IM) drive systems, knowledge of the stator currents is essential for implementing vector control structures. However, current sensors (CSs) may fail. This paper proposes a CS-FTC system which enables the detection and compensation of different CS failures. The modified Luenberger observer extended with simultaneous estimation of both winding resistances of the IM is used, which enables an accurate stator current reconstruction in the case of CS fault. In contrast to solutions known in the literature, the proposed approach utilizes a single observer, which allows for improved performance while simultaneously reducing computational requirements compared to dual observers and multi-observers.

articleTitle: Optimized Bus-Clamping Modulation Strategies for Dual-Inverter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: The Dual-Inverter (DI) emerges as a viable solution to address the ever-growing demands of electric drives, encompassing fault tolerance capability, waveform quality, superior DC-bus voltage utilization, and multilevel operation. The DI with isolated DC sources eliminates the path for zero sequence current (ZSC), thereby enabling the implementation of various modulation strategies. This paper introduces two bus-clamping modulation strategies aimed at minimizing switching losses for DI with isolated DC sources. The effectiveness of these modulation strategies is validated using a DI model in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, incorporating SiC MOS-FETs transistors parameterized in accordance with the manufacturer’s datasheet. An induction machine with a rated power of 12 kW serves as the load for DI.

articleTitle: Battery Charging Resonant Converter with a Secondary Side PFC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: A single-phase supplied Li-ion battery charger with a maximum voltage of 60 V, power of 600 W and with a PFC functionality is under development currently. The industrial partner especially accents EMI minimizing, which is a common problem of high-power switching supplies. Small size is required as well, therefore a relatively high switching frequency of approx. 150 kHz was chosen. To ensure a satisfactory efficiency and low EMI a resonant converter is used. The proposed novel design ensures lowering the dv/dt slope on the primary side of the resonant converter independently of the load to minimize EMI significantly. The resonant converter is supplied from a passive rectifier with a soft DC link (low capacitance in the DC link). This converter serves only for galvanic separation and voltage/current transformation, there is no voltage control and therefore ideal conditions for soft switching are ensured (both ZCS and ZVS). The output voltage control as well as the input phase current shaping (PFC functionality) are provided by an additional secondary step-up converter. Important aspects, simulations and design details are included in this contribution.

articleTitle: Creating an Energy-Efficient Óbuda University Blockchain in Education for Secure Data Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Blockchain technology is becoming more and more popular these days, despite this, many people are skeptical about it and even reject its use. Two years ago, famous people expressed their displeasure at the high energy requirements of blockchain technology to be sustainable, causing a huge backlash, and as a result, even the coin prices began to fall sharply. The aim of the research is to reveal which blockchain technology requires the least energy during its operation. As part of the practical implementation of the research, a private university blockchain will be created, which enables efficient data storage for educational institutions and requires less energy compared to so-called "traditional" blockchains. As a result of decentralized data storage, universities can store their sensitive data more securely compared to cloud-based centralized data storage, since they are saved and distributed on the nodes. To increase the energy efficiency of the blockchain, it is calculated which solar solution could reduce the energy cost of the blockchain's operation to a value close to zero.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning based Power Switch Fault Diagnosis in DC/DC Converters for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a robust approach to handle with the diagnosis of open-circuit and short-circuit faults in a DC/DC converter used for PV applications. The proposed approach uses only the measurements sent by the PV current and voltage sensors. Then after, a deep learning (DL) based classifier is built to detect the power-semiconductor fault and to discriminate open-circuit fault from short-circuit fault. In this work, a comparison between KNN, SVM, LSTM and BiLSTM models is discussed. Several simulations under MATLAB/Simulink software are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Comparative loss evaluation of SiC semiconductors and capacitors in 800-V DC-Link for NPC family structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: Power losses play a crucial role in the performance of an electric drive, and inverters are one of its constituent parts. This paper evaluates power losses and the possibility of increasing the power density by decreasing power losses, the size of the DC-link capacitors, and the number or size of the semiconductors. Besides the selection of components and operating switching frequency, the structure of an inverter affects the power density. Different kinds of capacitors and semiconductors are compared and analyzed in this paper in different 3-level inverter topologies. NPC, ANPC, and T-type NPC (TNPC) are compared in a range of switching frequencies from 10 kHz to 50 kHz to find the best topology, capacitor, and semiconductor in every single step of switching frequency. A constant thermal situation is considered to meet needed temperature restrictions and have a fair comparison. Simulations and calculations are performed for 800 V DC-Link voltage, 70 A peak output current NPC, ANPC, and TNPC inverters in MATLAB Simulink and PLECS blockset software linked together.

articleTitle: Systematic Design Method of a PMSM for EVs Using Analytical Characteristic Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a systematic design method for surface permanent magnet synchronous motors for variable speed operation system, such as in EVs, using various electromagnetic equations that determine the characteristics of the motor. In the proposed design method, accurate electric loading and magnet’s flux to meet the power requirements are determined using four geometric design variables. With the obtained two loadings, the detailed motor geometries are designed, and the winding specifications are determined. As a case study, various 4 kW PMSMs for EV are designed using the proposed method within the given range of four variables. Among various motor candidates designed, the model with the smallest volume is selected as the optimal model. Finally, the validity of the proposed method is verified by comparing the suggested analytical and FE analysis results of the selected 4kW SPM synchronous motor.

articleTitle: Simplified Thermal Analysis and CFD Simulation in Design Process of Power PCB Fitted with SMD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 21st International Power Electronics and Motion Control Conference (PEMC)
abstract: This article discusses power losses, heating, and heat distribution on high-power PCBs fitted with high-power SMD components. The paper presents two thermal design methods for power SMD PCBs, compares them with each other, and contrasts them with reference thermal measurements on a PCB prototype.
